html:
An earthquake of magnitude 6.8 that struck northern Armenia, then a Soviet republic, on 7 December 1988. The town of Spitak was almost wiped out, and the cities of Leninakan (now Gyumri) and Kirovakan were badly hit. Some 25,000 people died, and estimates run higher.

Many deaths came from badly built Soviet concrete apartment blocks that fell flat. Mikhail Gorbachev cut short a visit to the United States to fly to the disaster area. For the first time in decades the Soviet Union asked for and accepted large foreign aid, and rescue teams came from many countries.

The quake hit a republic already in turmoil over Nagorno-Karabakh, and the slow recovery added to anger with Moscow. Three years later the Soviet Union dissolved and Armenia rebuilt as an independent state.
